Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for the renewal call yesterday. As discussed, we're sending our proposed redlines for the MSA and an updated order form that reflects the capacity rebalance we need for Q3/Q4. Key asks from our side: an 18-month term (instead of 12), the ability to reallocate unused capacity across teams at quarter boundaries, and a one-time credit if monthly usage exceeds committed capacity during the first three months.

Attached: Novaprospects_MSA_redlines_v2.docx and OrderForm_Q3_Uplift.xlsx.

Also flagging that our Security team will follow up with standard SOC2 + data residency confirmations — expect an email from legal@novaprospects.com.

Appreciate a short timeline (ideally by early next week) so we can get this into our procurement cadence.

Best,

Thanks, Rishi / Sara — I've reviewed Novaprospects_MSA_redlines_v2.docx. High-level legal summary below and questions for Novaprospects: 

1) Term & termination: 18-month term is acceptable from Redwood's perspective provided the order form shows prorated billing and an explicit auto-renew clause is not reintroduced in the same section. We will insert language that caps retroactive credits and clarifies termination at the end of term.

2) SLA credit: Proposed 5% credit capped at one month of fees — OK as a commercial concession but need to convert to a clear calculation and cap in §4.3. Our concern: cumulative credits that exceed revenue for that month. We'll propose a per-incident calculation with a total monthly cap equal to the committed monthly fees.

3) Capacity reallocation: operationally fine; legal wants to avoid a catch-all transfer right that could allow resale. We will permit transfers between named internal business units and require notice at quarter boundary. Suggest adding a simple transfer table and a limit (e.g., 30% of committed capacity per quarter).

4) Data retention / audit logs: your redline removed the 24-month audit rights clause. Please confirm whether Novaprospects still needs audit access or only SOC2 reports. If audit rights remain, we'll need to narrow scope and schedule.

5) Indemnity/IP: You've added a mutual carveout on third-party model claims. We need to narrow that for open-source model usage; Redwood will accept a mutually narrowed clause limited to non-malicious third-party content.

I've attached a marked-up MSA (Laura_redline_MSA_v1.docx) with tracked changes and comments (minor commercial suggestions and three legal must-haves). Additionally, Marissa — please confirm operational impacts on transfers and the proposed 30% cap. Kimberly — can you produce the revised order form and a short amortization schedule?

I'll target a consolidated redline by Tue 16 Jul for Rishi to send to Novaprospects.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Head of Legal — Contracts | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Renewal packet - proposed MSA redlines and order form adjustments

Laura — thanks for the quick review and for the detailed notes. Answers inline below: 

> 1) Term & termination
We are fine with proration and no auto-renew. We just need the 18-month firm term to align with our budgeting (Q3 start).

> 2) SLA credit
We can accept the per-incident calculation you suggested; our ask is that the total monthly credit not be less than the value required to make our budgeting whole in a severe outage scenario. If you convert to a per-incident formula, can you also add an operational SLA recovery path (escalation to a named contact and remediation window)?

> 3) Capacity reallocation
Accept the 30% cap on transfers per quarter (great compromise). We will list the receiving business units by name in the order form.

> 4) Data retention / audit logs
Novaprospects is comfortable with SOC2 reports only — we do not require live audit access. The redline removed the 24-month audit clause intentionally.

> 5) Indemnity/IP
We accept narrowing the carveout language. Our legal team will send one short paragraph to fit the mutual carveout scope.

Operational ask: we still want a one-time capacity credit if usage exceeds committed capacity in the first three months post-renewal — please confirm if that will be recorded as a credit on the order form or handled as a billing adjustment in your AR process.

Tom Reyes (cc) will be our procurement lead for signature routing — he needs a final order form and a statement of any one-off credits to route through Novaprospects' PO process.

Thanks — Sara

Sara / Tom — thanks for the clarifications and for accepting the compromise language. Summary of path forward and agreed items (so procurement has a clean checklist):

1) Term: 18 months, effective 1 Aug 2029. No auto-renew clause. Billing prorated across first invoice.
2) Capacity reallocation: transfers between named internal business units; cap = 30% of committed monthly capacity per quarter. Transfer notification required 10 business days before quarter boundary.
3) SLA credit: use per-incident calculation with a monthly cap equal to committed monthly fees (legal will draft formula and an escalation path to include a named contact and remediation windows).
4) One-time capacity credit: Redwood will apply a one-time credit if monthly usage exceeds committed capacity during the first three months post-renewal. Commercial will record as a credit on the order form (line item: One-time Onboarding Overage Credit). We will show the credit on the pro forma invoice; Kimberly to include in the order form.
5) Data/audit: Novaprospects will accept SOC2 reports only; no live audit access required.
6) Indemnity carveout: legal will accept the narrowed mutual carveout and will incorporate the short paragraph Novaprospects legal sends.

Next steps: 
- Kimberly to post a revised OrderForm_Q3_Uplift.xlsx with the One-time Onboarding Overage Credit and an amortization schedule by Mon 15 Jul.
- Laura to consolidate the MSA redline incorporating the narrowed carveout and the SLA formula by Tue 16 Jul.
- Rishi will send the consolidated packet to Novaprospects (DocuSign link included) for procurement review on Wed 17 Jul.

If that matches your expectations, Tom — please confirm routing and target signature window. Happy to hop on a 15-min call if procurement needs a faster turnaround.

Thanks all,
